page.overview:
Who is Charlie Nash?

Charlie was created as the victim whose death Guile was avenging during the Street Fighter II series. What was most interesting was that this character did not have a face, only a name when being mentioned in 1991. In fact even the developers at Capcom didn't know what Charlie looked like originally. In some unused art of Super Street Fighter II by Bengus the only photo that Guile had of his friend wearing the same green tank-top, however his face isn't visible due to the photo being partially burnt. Making him the original gaming unknown soldier.

Players were questioning if Charlie was a friend or family member who was murdered in the line of duty. Guile would hoist his dog tags in the air in some victory animations. The myth behind Charlie grew as the endings in the Street Fighter II were changed and new details were added. In the English-scripted ending, Guile accuses M. Bison of the murder of his dear friend Charlie in Cambodia; this plot element was added to give Guile's backstory more character development. Since The World Warrior, Guile would threaten M. Bison; but in Super Street Fighter II Turbo, Guile would visit the grave of his friend. Guile is a visually unique character, with his military look and tall haircut, but he became interesting thanks to his ending. He attacked M. Bison after his defeat, grabbing him by the collar. It was a palpable rage when he brought up the names of Charlie and Cambodia. Audiences didn't know quite what happened but it sounded like a serious incident occurred several years ago. When Charlie Nash was killed, Guile was less muscular, considered by M. Bison as a runt, Only Guile's wife and daughter were able to talk him out of killing M. Bison. Some of the endings in the game were silly (such as Blanka, Zangief, and Dhalsim), but most were played out like a dramatic movie, Guile's ending was no exception. He had abandoned his family in the pursuit of revenge and was reunited once his vendetta was completed.

When Charlie debut in Street Fighter Alpha: Warriors' Dreams in 1995, much like how Guile's hairstyle was inspired by both Jean-Pierre Polnareff and Rudolf von Stroheim, Nash's was inspired by Polnareff's teammate, Noriaki Kakyoin.

Of course many Capcom fans with a keen-eye have pointed out that the official design of Charlie bares a striking resemblance to Dave the scientist. He was one of the alien henchmen characters from Cyberbots: Fullmetal Madness. He served under Princess Devilotte de Deathsatan IX, an over-the-top lolita-dressed alien bent on universal domination. It is noticeable that the same hair and glasses on both characters. Dave debuted a few months before Charlie, it's entirely possible that the artists liked the look of the character and incorporated some of his visual cues on Charlie as well.
